Classical harmonic oscillators (Fig. 4.9) vibrate at a natural frequency that is determined by Equation 20.9; they can vibrate with any amplitude (and energy, therefore) but the energies of quantum harmonic oscillators are restricted to fixed values as we now show.

The energies and wave functions for the quantum harmonic oscillator model are obtained by solving the one-dimensional Schrödinger equation with the har- monic oscillator potential energy term added to the kinetic energy term.
